claims.claim: visual cross discrimination varies perceptual load
claims.limits: high vs low load defined by arm length vs color; not daily stress

claims.claim: 2011 experiment 1 participants aware 21/28 low and 7/28 high
claims.limits: 2011 Exp1 critical-trial detection among 28 participants per group, not repeated trial proportion; separate Exp2 high-load 19/24 miss (79%) and Exp3 distinct task

claims.claim: 2011 max 79% miss in high load
claims.limits: max across tested conditions, not population rate

claims.claim: the tone was a short stimulus embedded in white noise
claims.limits: timing and headphone setup, not proof of missed alarms in normal life

claims.claim: Auditory gorilla is a spoken male intrusion audible for 19 seconds; full-scene attentive repeat, not isolated sound
claims.limits: Attentive replay involved COMPLETE auditory scene, male voice and unusual-events listening; not universal population rate

claims.claim: 2015 Raveh four experiments including 50-percent tone-present condition
claims.limits: Exp2 auditory-response-first and Exp3 50% tone-present are different manipulations; signal sensitivity and criterion distinct

claims.claim: auditory sensitivity can diminish with high visual load
claims.limits: lab effect; not clinical hearing loss

claims.claim: 2015 Molloy MEG early auditory responses altered about 100 ms
claims.limits: Separate MEG analyzed n=13 and behavioral analyzed n=10; not simultaneous individual auditory reports

claims.claim: P3 response and detection also reduced
claims.limits: Later MEG P3 and separate behavioral tone detection; cannot treat as one group

claims.claim: Puységur links are historical context only
claims.limits: not hypnosis efficacy evidence

claims.claim: Focus page existing 52-page workbook and Jetpack lead path
claims.limits: live page verified; individual signup confirmation not independently observed

claims.limits: not independently delivered/tested

claims.limits: not independently tested

claims.limits: never imply a clinical outcome

claims.claim: Macdonald Lavie findings establish effectiveness of Zen12
